linkedin.documentTitle: The Roof Replacement Week, Day by Day
linkedin.text:
Peak replacement season is here, and the most common thing we hear from homeowners is that nobody ever told them what the week would actually look like. So we wrote it down: the dumpster's arrival, the loud day, the decking inspection, the layer-by-layer rebuild, and the magnet sweep at the end.

What 10+ years on Portland metro roofs taught us is that surprises happen under old roofs, but surprise bills shouldn't. That's why decking gets inspected sheet by sheet on day one, with photos and per-sheet pricing the homeowner saw in writing before the job started. And why a rain pause isn't a crisis; the underlayment stage is built to be left watertight overnight.

The full day-by-day guide is on our site, and the roof assessment is free: https://www.frenchroofing.com/estimate

gmb: Wondering what actually happens during a roof replacement? Most take one to three days. The day before, a dumpster arrives and shingles get delivered. Day one is tear-off, the loud part, where the crew strips the roof to bare plywood and inspects every sheet of decking for rot; if there's damage, you hear about it that day with photos and per-sheet pricing you saw in writing beforehand. The new roof then goes on as a system: ice-and-water membrane, underlayment, drip edge, new flashing at every penetration, and shingles nailed to manufacturer spec, with ridge venting to finish. If Oregon weather interrupts, the underlayment stage stays watertight overnight. The job ends with a raked yard, cleared gutters, a magnet sweep of the lawn and driveway for stray nails, and a walkthrough with photos and your warranty paperwork.
